items.wrong: It was raining, because we stayed home.
items.fix: It was raining, so we stayed home.
items.why: So gives the result; because gives the reason.

items.wrong: Although it rained, but we went out.
items.fix: Although it rained, we went out.
items.why: Do not use although and but together.

items.wrong: We stayed home because was raining.
items.fix: We stayed home because it was raining.
items.why: After because, use a subject: it.

teach.goal: Como não traduzir palavra por palavra.

Peça que digam a forma natural em voz alta.
extra90: Cada aluno cria um erro típico seu e o grupo corrige.

facts.label: Conectores de ideia
facts.sub: Use so para o resultado, because para a razão, but e although para o contraste. Cada conector liga duas ideias completas.

facts.label: Então
facts.sub: Use so para o resultado: It was raining, so we stayed home. Em geral há uma vírgula antes de so. A razão vem primeiro e o resultado depois.

facts.label: Porque
facts.sub: Use because para a razão: We stayed home because it was raining. Depois de because, use sujeito e verbo. Não use because of com frase completa.

pages.title: A rainy weekend · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a gray Sunday morning in a cozy house in Dallas. Thunder rolls outside, and rain hits the roof. A board game and a half puzzle sit on the table. Nina comes to visit her friend Carla. Carla looks pale and wears a thick sweater. They sit down and start to talk.
“Nina, did you go to the lake on Saturday?” says Carla. “No. It was raining, so we stayed home.” says Nina. “Oh no. Were the kids sad because they could not go?” says Carla.
